messages:
alex: Heads-up — proposing we add lightweight route provenance stamps to the policy engine so every decision can emit a compact 'why' for explainability + audits. sketch: ordered list of applied rules, intermediate scores, tie-breaker id, and final model/variant.

maria: +1 for explainability but worried about telemetry volume. how big are these stamps?

alex: goal is < 1kb per sampled request. Not full traces for all traffic — default sampling 0.1% with opt-in for debug cohorts.

siva: Can we make the stamp deterministic and replayable? e.g., canonicalize inputs and include a short decision hash so reproducing a decision is simple.

ken: deterministic hash is good. Also we should include an `explain_id` that the Console can fetch, rather than dumping everything inline. Keeps logs small.

maria: fetching on-demand means retention + query infra. ops: ops here — concerns: provenance may contain tenant hints or prompt prefixes. we must strip sensitive data and ensure KMS access controls for explain fetches.

alex: agreed on redaction. Proposal: stamps contain only rule ids, numeric scores, short enums, and a 16-byte base64 decision-hash. no raw prompt text. if full replay requested (for debug), use a controlled archive flow with consent and access audit.

siva: implementation note: policy engine already produces per-rule incremental score. we can emit two artifacts: (1) compact stamp (for events/metrics), (2) verbose trace written to secure blobstore only on sampled/explicit requests.

ken: API surface: add `?explain=stamp` and `?explain=trace` on debug routes. default returns `stamp` header: `x-route-stamp: v1:base64hash` and minimal JSON in telemetry. Console can call `/explain/{explain_id}` to fetch blob (RBAC checked).

maria: what about performance? extra serialization and string work in hot path could add p95. we should benchmark.

deploy-bot: unit tests: policy_stamps: ok. perf-check: baseline 18ms p95, with stamp-serial 19.2ms p95 (dev cluster).

ops: 1. add redaction rules + schema review 2. ensure explain blobs go to encrypted bucket 3. define TTL and retention policy 4. sampling controls per-tenant.

alex: next steps I propose: write a short RFC covering stamp schema (rule id, short reason code, numeric score, decision-hash, model-variant), sampling defaults, trace blob format, redaction rules, and Console integration endpoints. volunteers? @maria @siva?

maria: I can take schema + Console UI bits.

siva: I can prototype runtime emission + deterministic hashing.

ken: i'll draft the API endpoints and RBAC notes.

ops: i'll draft the retention/KMS checklist.

alex: sweet. I'll assemble an initial RFC draft and link it tomorrow: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/route-provenance. Please add comments there. :thumbsup: 

maria: tiny thought — include a `confidence_penalty` field when we fall back to cheaper models so Console can surface quality regressions.

alex: good call, add that to schema.

ken: can we also expose a compact histogram of score contributors (top-3) to keep stamp <1kb?

siva: yes, top-3 contributor ids + their weights is enough for most cases.

alex: ok that's the plan. we'll aim for an RFC by EOD Friday and a perf canary next week. thanks all!
